title: test(app-shell): useDeferredFirstSend waits on the replay, not a fixed tick
body:
Fixes #36967
Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 用户无感:只改了一个测试文件里「等待自动补发首条消息」的写法,产品代码一行未动。
- 属于合并队列稳定性:这个测试在繁忙的队列机器上偶发失败,曾把一个 p1 修复踢出合并队列,这里替开发席位清掉这个绊脚石。
- 出错的影响只在测试层:最坏是这个测试仍偶发失败、需要重新排队,可直接撤回本 PR,对用户和数据都没有影响。
- 无。

## What changes

`ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/ai/__tests__/useDeferredFirstSend.test.tsx` only. The `flushReplay()` helper, which waited on its own `setTimeout(0)`, is gone; every call site now waits on a condition:

- **Steps that should replay** (12 sites) wait with `waitFor` on the exact observable the next assertion reads: `doSend`'s call count or its call arguments, or, in the StrictMode case, the stash being consumed (`pendingRef.current` null; the timer clears the stash and sends in the same task).
- **Steps that must NOT replay** (2 sites: the `c2` id change after a consumed send, and the targeted stash held by a mismatched pane) cannot use `waitFor`, because a `waitFor` on a negative passes before the replay has had its chance. They run through a new helper, `actThenRunPendingTimers(step)`: fake `setTimeout`/`clearTimeout` only, `act(step)`, then `act(vi.runOnlyPendingTimers)`, then real timers again in a `finally`. Any replay timer the step armed has fired before the negative assertion reads.

No assertion is removed or loosened, there are no retries, and nothing is skipped. Where a `waitFor` now holds the first assertion of a block, that assertion has moved into the `waitFor` and is not repeated after it. RTL's `asyncWrapper` ends every `waitFor` with its own `setTimeout(0)` drain, so an exactly-once count read after a `waitFor` still sees any sibling timer that fired in the same tick.

Why the old wait raced: the hook arms the replay from a `useEffect` with `setTimeout(0)`. In the conversation-create cases, `setConversationId('conv-1')` lands after `await res.json()` inside `waitFor`, where RTL has turned act off. React 19 then runs the remounted pane's passive effects as a later scheduler task, so on a starved runner the test's `setTimeout(0)` could be registered before the replay timer was armed. The test's timer then fired first, and `doSend` read 0 calls (queue run 45373444137, `Test UI (7/16)`). No product change is needed: the product's ordering is correct, and only the test's wait was too short.

Read first (by risk):
1. `actThenRunPendingTimers` and its comment block near the top of the file: the only new mechanism. Check that it restores real timers in `finally`.
2. `mounting creates nothing; the first send creates one row and is replayed into it`: the case that failed in the queue.
3. `the replayed first send survives the effect teardown StrictMode runs on mount`: the wait moved from the abort check to stash consumption.

## Tests

All local readings are on head `c2c6bbd1223`. Each section below folds its log excerpts.

<details><summary>30 repeated runs of the file: 30/30 green</summary>

`bash os-verify-lock.sh -- bash loop.sh 30`, where each iteration runs `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/app-shell/src/console/ai/__tests__/useDeferredFirstSend.test.tsx` from `ui/`:

```
run 1 exit=0       Tests  15 passed (15)
...
run 30 exit=0       Tests  15 passed (15)
TALLY pass=30 fail=0 of 30
os-verify-lock: VERDICT command-exit 0
```
</details>

<details><summary>Under CPU load: 10/10 green (six busy loops on 4 cores, one fork, load average 9.4 to 14.1)</summary>

The setup mirrors the seat's diagnosis run: six busy loops (recorded PIDs, killed by trap), and `vitest run --pool forks --maxWorkers=1` on the file, ten times, under the lock. Other agents' work was also running on the same box.

```
load before runs: 6.46 5.81 5.59
load-run 1 exit=0       Tests  15 passed (15) · loadavg 14.08
...
load-run 10 exit=0       Tests  15 passed (15) · loadavg 9.47
TALLY-LOAD pass=10 fail=0 of 10
os-verify-lock: VERDICT command-exit 0
```

A green run under load cannot prove the race is closed: the old file also passed 31 local runs. The mutation run below is the deterministic evidence.
</details>

<details><summary>One-off mutations (not committed): the new waits are conditions and the negative drain can fail</summary>

Both mutations ran through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor hit x1, blob changed, restore proven: blob == HEAD and `git diff HEAD` empty). They touch the product file only for the duration of the run.

**Leg A: replay delayed from 0 ms to 50 ms** (`AiChatPage.tsx` replay timer `}, 0);` changed to `}, 50);`). This is the queue failure made deterministic: the replay timer fires after any fixed `setTimeout(0)`. The origin/main copy of this test file was run beside the new one, from a temporary sibling file that was deleted afterwards.

```
NEW_EXIT=0       Tests  15 passed (15)
BASE_EXIT=1       Tests  12 failed | 3 passed (15)
     × mounting creates nothing; the first send creates one row and is replayed into it
     × replays the first message across the id-keyed pane REMOUNT (reproduces the reported bug)
     ... (all 12 replay cases)
```

**Leg B: the targeted-stash guard deleted** (a mismatched pane now replays). This checks that `actThenRunPendingTimers` really fires the replay timer before the negative assertion reads, so the check cannot pass trivially:

```
NEW_EXIT=1       Tests  1 failed | 14 passed (15)
     × holds a targeted stash in a mismatched-agent pane, replays it in the matching one
AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times
```
</details>

<details><summary>app-shell type-check: green (both tsc programs, edited file compiled)</summary>

`pnpm exec turbo run type-check --concurrency=2 --filter=@object-ui/app-shell`, under the lock. It builds the `^build` closure first, then runs `tsc --noEmit` followed by `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`.

```
@object-ui/app-shell:type-check: cache miss, executing 70efc8ea30bbbe0f
 Tasks:    69 successful, 69 total
os-verify-lock: VERDICT command-exit 0
```

`tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFilesOnly` lists the edited file (1 hit among 6941 files), so this reading covers it.

My first attempt, a bare `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` without the `@object-ui/*` dists built, exited 2 on TS2307 "cannot find module" cascades. That was a missing build, not a type-check verdict, so I re-ran it through turbo as above.
</details>

## Acceptance notes

- The `await act(async () => {})` lines in the three conversation-create cases ("let the mount-time resolve settle") are left as they are. They are act-scope flushes, not timer waits. On the cache-miss path the mount resolve runs synchronously inside the effect, so these lines race nothing. The assertion that follows them is a negative ("mounting creates nothing"), which no condition wait could express.
- The full `@object-ui/app-shell` test suite (2416 files) is left to CI's `Test UI` (16 shards). Locally I ran only the edited file, plus the derived gate families below.

## Verification

Two-minute check: from `ui/`, run `pnpm exec vitest run packages/app-shell/src/console/ai/__tests__/useDeferredFirstSend.test.tsx`. Expect `Tests  15 passed (15)`.

<details><summary>Derived gate families: 27/27 run, all exit 0</summary>

The list comes from `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`: 27 commands for the one changed path. Each was run on `c2c6bbd1223`, with its exit code captured before any pipe. Reconciliation:

```
Run reconciliation — 27 derived, 27 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN.
✓ dispatch-gates --ran: 27 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 27 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED zero — all 27 recorded an exit code and none of them is 3).
```

`pnpm --dir ui exec vitest run scripts/`: `Test Files  172 passed | 2 skipped (174)`, `Tests  5129 passed | 2 skipped (5131)`.

No changeset: `@object-ui/app-shell` is `private: true`, and its `files` list (`dist`, `src/styles.css`, README, CHANGELOG, LICENSE) does not ship tests. The PR therefore carries `skip-changeset`.
</details>
